The broken window fallacy is not about literal broken windows; it uses that situation as an analogy. It is an argument supporting the idea that inefficient use of resources robs economies of productivity. You must realize that every individual has a certain productive capacity (labor or otherwise), and that killing that person creates a deficit in productive work. While subsistence farming has very low productive value, that productive value is greater than zero (which is the productive value of a person dead from plague...in fact a person dead from plague may have less than productive capacity than zero, as a plague-ridden corpse could infect others, potentially killing them). You're also missing the opportunities that the dead person could create (new ideas, inventions, innovations, or just increasing the population so that more potential productivity is added to the overall pool).

But the broken window fallacy is indeed about literal broken windows, although it can be induced to a more general case, such as any destruction of property or wealth.
